title: Microrelease activation lattice and hotseat notes (WIP)
summary: Working notes and pragmatic checklist for microreleases that interleave canary slices and small-scale A/B experiments. Focused on cross-functional handoffs, fast rollback, and minimizing blast radius for LLM features.
purpose: Create a compact, usable playbook for product + SRE + infra + support to run frequent microreleases (tiny traffic windows) with clear stewarding and a designated "hotseat" rotation. Capture templates, thresholds, and operational gotchas for teams launching model/serving changes.
scope: Applies to: feature-gated model changes, routing policy tweaks, inference config (quantization/batching), and UI-introduced behavior changes that require traffic exposure. Not for infra-wide capacity migrations or major schema changes.
definitions: microrelease: a deliberate, small-traffic activation (0.1% - 5%) meant to validate behavior and telemetry quickly
hotseat: the designated on-call rotation for a microrelease window; acts as the immediate responder and runbook owner
steward: product or feature owner responsible for decisioning and coordinating stakeholders during activation
preconditions: All tickets/PRs linked and merged to main, feature flag present with unique key
Test harness run against canary model for representative prompts (smoke + quality probes) within last 24h
SRE signed off on resource budgets and predicted token QPS for the window
Support and comms notified (email + #release-room on Slack) with time and rollback channel
Observability baseline snapshot captured (P95 latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-request)
activation_lattice: We think of activation as a lattice of orthogonal slices: user cohort (new vs returning), geography/region, client platform (web/mobile/API), query complexity (short vs long), and traffic tier (paid/free). Build microreleases by combining 2–3 axes to keep cardinality low (eg. mobile x EU x complex-queries = 0.5% global).
rollout_steps: Prep: create release note in Confluence + link Jira (CON-xxxx). Upload quick checklist to #release-room
Stage: enable feature flag for internal beta or synthetic traffic and sweep basic smoke probes (5–10 minutes)
Canary: enable for tiny cohort (0.1–0.5%) with full telemetry, run for 10–15 minutes
Observe: run automated QA prompts and monitor P95/P99 latency, token-per-response, rerank-safety metrics, and user-facing errors
Scale: if stable for 30m and no quality regressions, expand to 1–3% and continue observation
A/B: run parallel A/B if testing behavior variants; keep variant sizes small and pre-register hypothesis
Full: only after 24–72h of stable signals and stakeholder signoff, increase exposure per product roadmap
Cleanup: close runbook, annotate telemetry anomalies, and schedule retrospective within 3 business days
metrics_and_alerts: Latency: P95 > baseline * 1.20 -> alert to #sre-llm and hotseat
Errors: client-facing error rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute or 3x relative -> immediate abort
Quality: automated eval set: BLEU/ROUGE-like surrogate or scoring drop > 5% absolute on canary set -> flag for product
Unit-cost: token-cost-per-response increase > 15% without latency improvement -> investigate routing/quantization
Fallbacks: fallback model count (per-minute) > 10 -> investigate upstream capacity or policy misconfiguration
abort_criteria: Any P99 request that results in an un-recoverable 5xx spike (>3x baseline)
Human-sensed quality regression reported by support within the first 60 minutes
Safety signal: automated classifier triggers > 0.1% of outputs with sensitive content violations
Telemetry gap: missing critical metrics for > 5 minutes (cannot make informed decision)
escalation_path: Hotseat -> Steward (product) -> On-call SRE -> Infra Eng Lead -> Director of Product (if rollback rejected)
For safety incidents: Hotseat -> Safety Reviewer -> Legal (if PII/exfiltration risk) -> Exec on-call
Use Slack channel: #release-room for operational updates, escalate to #oncall-escalation if aborting
communication_templates: Slack: @here Microrelease START: feature=<flag> steward=<name> hotseat=<name> window=10:00-10:30 UTC. Watch P95 & quality-set. Rollback channel: #release-room
Slack abort: ABORT: microrelease <flag> rolled back at <time> due to <reason>. Hotseat notes: <short bullet>. Follow-up: retrospective scheduled <date>
Email to CS: Heads up - small activation happening <date/time>. Expected impact: 0.5% of traffic. If customer escalations come in, please tag #release-room and ping hotseat.
experiments_examples: Example A/B: Reranker-v2 vs Reranker-v1 on paid users, cohort size 1% global, hypothesis: +4% NDCG on search intents within 72h
Example microrelease: switch KV-cache partitioning to async flush for long chat sessions on EU-mobile complex queries, start 0.2% -> scale if stable
Interleaved canary+A/B: enable model variant A for 0.2% and variant B for 0.2% of total traffic (separate cohorts) to compare cost vs latency tradeoffs
telemetry_hints: Always capture a baseline snapshot (export dashboards) 1 hour before activation
Synthetic probes: include cold-start, high-token and adversarial prompt probes in the smoke suite
Correlate user complaints with trace ids: add quick query param trace_id to sampled requests during the window
Instrument token-cost tag on each request to track sudden per-request inflation
operational_tips: If you expect capacity hiccups, pre-warm the fallback pool and pin a low-cost model as an auto-fallback
Keep the steward small: max 3 decision-makers to avoid coordination lag
During holidays or large external events, avoid microreleases that touch conversational safety classifiers
For mobile SDK rollouts, coordinate with SDK team to ensure consistent client flag behavior and playback
open_questions: Do we want a formal 'blast-radius calculator' that recommends cohort sizes based on historical variance? (TODO: meet with Data Science)
Should hotseat rotation be part of weekly oncall or separate rotation? pros/cons documented below
How much synthetic traffic is permissible so we don't skew product metrics (sales/eng want larger windows for faster signal)
bottom_notes: Notes-to-self: run a dry-run with synthetic traffic next Tuesday 14:00 UTC. Follow up items: (1) ask DS for variance report; (2) update #release-room template to include 'safety classifier rate' by default.
